reason:
Not the refuted arrival-animation request in new clothes - it genuinely asks for no motion - but it fails on composition, on three measured grounds.

(1) The premise is factually incomplete. Measured at 390x844 and 1440x960, the terminus is not 'separated from an errand only by weight': it carries the ONLY full-measure hairline in the composition (.b-item[data-anchor]::before, left:-23px to right:0, top:-16px), the rail visibly terminates beneath it, its title steps 400->600, and its count column reads 79 - the identical figure the reader carried down 1,692px from the 96px horizon count. The arrival rhymes with the horizon by restating its number at the foot. That is a designed terminus, not an unmarked row.

(2) The day's magnitude is deliberately at the head, and the fix inverts the lock's stated order. The lock: 'the count, the date and what the day is are the first three things on the surface, in that order.' Measured, those are: 96px/148px count, .b-when at 20px (phone) / 30px (desk and print), .b-sub 'Wedding day' at 15px/400 at 0.62. The last row's title text is VERBATIM the same string, 'Wedding day' - it appears exactly twice on the surface. The fix would render the second, list-position statement at 30/600 full ink: twice the size, heavier and brighter than the horizon's own naming of the day, making the horizon's third element the smallest and dimmest statement of the phrase on the page. At >=701px it would also tie .b-when at 30px and beat it on weight, so a list row out-ranks the ceremonial date. The finding guards only the 96px count and leaves the second and third of the three unguarded. On the printed sheet - which the fix explicitly includes - the two statements sit on ONE page simultaneously (measured: .b-sub y=393, anchor row y=792, horizon left, measure right), so the keepsake would print 'Wedding day' small-and-grey beside 'Wedding day' at headline size. That is the same defect class the panel already refuted for the editor's reserved band: printing one name twice at fighting sizes inside one field of view.

(3) The proposed selector does not scale to a real wedding day. data-anchor is written per-row by DATE equality (render-b.js:143, item.date === F.project.primaryDate.date), not by 'last row', and the design explicitly builds for several moments on one date (data-stack lead/follow, rows divided by a 1px hairline, one tick and one count for the run). The fixture happens to hold exactly one moment on 3 October. A real ceremony/photographs/dinner/first-dance day would render three or four stacked rows at 30/600, one pixel apart, each at the ramp step the lock reserves for 'a screen's own headline'. The rule is right only for this fixture.

The ramp step itself is the last problem: 30 is --size-title, declared in the lock as 'a screen's own headline', and 20-48 is 'voice'. Putting a list item into the voice register is the composition saying the row is the screen. The screen is the horizon.
sharpenedFix: None. If a seat still feels the terminus is under-felt, the honest lever is the space around it, not the type: the rail already dies below the row, and the run-out beneath the last tick before the 'Behind you' fold could be given more air so the measure ends rather than stops. That is polish inside the existing ramp and does not restate the day's name at a larger size than the horizon does.
